newsitem.title: UK: London gold and silver lower, may weaken further.
newsitem.headline: London gold and silver lower, may weaken further.

text.p: The precious metals were weaker on Tuesday morning and some dealers and analysts predicted they may decline still further in the near term.
"The whole sector is looking relatively sickly but whether it's weak enough to go lower or just be capped on the upside we'll have to see," a dealers said.
Gold was off slightly following selling overnight, probably on behalf of gold producers, dealers said.
It was fixed at $382.35 an ounce compared to $382.90 on Monday afternoon and a London close of $383.10/$383.60.
But prices were expected to remain stuck in a tight range ahead of the expiry of options later in the day, which could provide some fresh direction to the rangebound market.
Options provide the right but not the obligation to buy or sell metal at a given price.

"We might see a bit of a battle later because it's right in the middle of the two key levels -- $380 and $385," a dealer said. "But I don't now if it has the legs to go in either direction. It might be a $381.50-$383 day," the dealer said.
Selling pressure may be offset slightly by the start of the peak demand time for gold, due to top consumer India's forthcoming Diwali festival of lights and wedding season.

On the price charts, however, gold's recent recovery above the key $380 support level looked likely to run out of steam soon, heralding the resumption of a downtrend which started in February, technical analysts said.
"While the downtrend is intact, I go with the view that this is a correction (higher)," said Karen Jones, technical analyst at Credit Suisse in London.
"The downtrend resistance line is at $384.95, so that is the break-out point. There is scope to test it, but I would be looking for a failure," she added.
Silver was also slightly easier at $4.89/$4.91 an ounce, a decline of three cents from Monday's London close.
But the weakest metal in the precious metals complex appeared to be platinum, hovering close to par with the price of gold since Friday for the first time nearly three years.
A week ago platinum was at around a $2 premium to gold.
Palladium also looked sickly, trading near recent lows at $115.50/$116.50 an ounce, down 50 cents from Monday's close.

Both platinum and palladium have been undermined in recent months by ample supplies from major producer Russia and slack demand from Japan's key electronics industry. --Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
